translation.title: Commentary on Sūrat "al-Ikhlāṣ." In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of God, glorified be His praise and hallowed be His names:
Say: He is God, One (1) God, the
(2) He neither begets nor is begotten (3) and there is none comparable to Him (4)
It is reported that the polytheists asked the Messenger of God ﷺ about the lineage of the Lord of Might, so God sent down this sūra as an answer to them.
Some said: rather it was revealed because the Jews asked him, saying to him: "This is God who created creation; who created God?" So it was revealed as an answer to them.
Mention of those who said it was revealed as an answer to the polytheists, who asked him to trace the lineage of the Lord, blessed and exalted:

c: Aḥmad b. Manīʿ al-Marwazī and Maḥmūd b. Khidāsh al-Ṭālaqānī told us, both said: Abū [Saʿd al-Ṣaghānī] [Fn 1] told us, he said: Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī told us, from al-Rabīʿ b. Anas, from Abū al-ʿĀliya, from Ubayy b. Kaʿb.
m: He said: The polytheists said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Trace for us the lineage of your Lord." So God sent down:
Say: He is God, One (1) God, the

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Yaḥyā b. Wāḍiḥ told us, he said: al-Ḥusayn told us, from Yazīd, from ʿIkrima.
m: He said: The polytheists said: "Muḥammad [Fn 1], tell us about your Lord; describe your Lord to us: what is He, and of what thing is He?" So God sent down:
to the end of the sūra. [Fn 2]

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Abū Jaʿfar, from al-Rabīʿ, from Abū al-ʿĀliya.
m: Say: He is God, One (1) God, the
: he said: The leaders of the confederates (
) said that: "Trace for us your Lord." Then Gabriel came to him with this. [Fn 3]

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAwf told me, he said: Surayj [Fn 4] told us, he said: Ismāʿīl b. Mujālid told us, from Mujālid, from al-Shaʿbī, from Jābir.
m: He said: The polytheists said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Trace for us your Lord." So God, blessed and exalted, sent down:

x: Mention of those who said it was revealed because of the question of the Jews:

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Salama told us, he said: Ibn Isḥāq told me, from Muḥammad, from Saʿīd.
m: He said: A group of the Jews came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Muḥammad, this is God who created creation; who created Him?" The Prophet ﷺ became angry until his color changed [Fn 1], and then he turned upon them [Fn 2] in anger for his Lord. Gabriel ؑ came to him and calmed him and said: "Lower your wing for yourself, Muḥammad." The answer to what they had asked came to him from God. He said: God says:

. When the Prophet ﷺ had recited it to them, they said: "Describe your Lord to us: how is His creation, how is His upper arm, how is His forearm?" The Prophet ﷺ became angrier than at his first anger and turned upon them in anger. Gabriel came to him and said to him the like of his earlier words, and brought him the answer to what they had asked:

And they did not appraise God with true appraisal, while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection and the heavens will be rolled up in His right hand. Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Saʿīd b. Abī ʿArūba, from Qatāda.
m: He said: Some of the Jews came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Trace for us your Lord." So
was revealed until the end of the sūra. [Fn 4]

x: If the matter is as we have described, the interpretation of the speech is: say, Muḥammad, to these people who ask you about the lineage of your Lord, His description and who created Him: the Lord about whom you asked me is God, to whom belongs the worship of everything. Worship is not fitting for anyone but Him and does not suit anything besides Him.
The people of Arabic differed about what governs the nominative
. One of them said [Fn 5]: what governs it is
is a pronoun of the situation (
Indeed, it is I, God, the Mighty, the Wise
[al-Naml 27:9]. Another of them said [Fn 6]: rather it is nominative, though indefinite, by way of a new start, as in
[Fn 7] ("this is my husband, an old man"). He said that
is an answer to the speech of a people who said to him: "What is it that you worship?" He said: "He is God." Then it was said to him: "What is He?" He said: "He is One."
could be followed by a new start unless it is preceded by one of the particles of doubt, such as
and its like. This second view is more in keeping with the doctrines of Arabic.

The correct reading in our view is with

for it, which spares us the need to cite anything else for its soundness. We have already explained the meaning of

evidence.text: When the Prophet ﷺ had recited it to them, they said: "Describe your Lord to us: how is His creation, how is His upper arm, how is His forearm?"
The reciters differed in reading it.

The general body of the reciters of the regions read {*aḥadun* (1) *Allāhu l-ṣamad*} with *tanwīn* on {*aḥad*}, except Naṣr b. ʿĀṣim and ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Isḥāq, from whom it is reported that they omitted the *tanwīn*: (*aḥadu Llāhu*) [Fn 1].
It seems that whoever read it so said: the nūn of inflection is sometimes dropped when it is followed by *alif-lām* or a quiescent letter, as the poet said [Fn 2]:
The correct reading in our view is with *tanwīn*, for two reasons.
The second is the consensus of the authoritative reciters of the regions in choosing *tanwīn* for it, which spares us the need to cite anything else for its soundness.

Mention of those who said this:

c: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. al-Aswad told us, he said: Muḥammad b. Rabīʿa told us, from Salama b. Sābūr, from ʿAṭiyya, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
m: : the one who is not hollow. [Fn 1]

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told us, he said: Sufyān told us, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid.
Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid.
al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Waraqāʾ told us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid.
m: : the solid that has no cavity. [Fn 4]

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Wakīʿ told us, both said: Sufyān told us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid.
m: : the one who has no cavity. [Fn 1]

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us. And Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us. Both from Sufyān, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid.
Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told us, he said: al-Rabīʿ b. Muslim told us, from al-Ḥasan.
m: : the one who has no cavity. [Fn 2]

c: He said: al-Rabīʿ b. Muslim told us, from Ibrāhīm b. Maysara.
m: He said: Mujāhid sent me to Saʿīd b. Jubayr to ask him about
. He said: "The one who has no cavity." [Fn 3]

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: Yaḥyā told us, he said: Ismāʿīl b. Abī Khālid told us, from al-Shaʿbī.
m: : the one who does not eat food. [Fn 4]

c: Yaʿqūb told us, he said: Hushaym told us, from Ismāʿīl b. Abī Khālid, from al-Shaʿbī.
m: : the one who does not eat food and does not drink drink. [Fn 5]

c: Abū Kurayb and Ibn Bashshār told us, both said: Wakīʿ told us, from Salama b. Nubayṭ, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
m: : the one who has no cavity. [Fn 6]

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Abī Zāʾida told us, from Ismāʿīl, from ʿĀmir.
m: : the one who does not eat food.

c: Ibn Bashshār and Zayd b. Akhzam told us, both said: Ibn Dāwūd told us, from al-Mustaqīm b. ʿAbd al-Malik, from Saʿīd b. al-Musayyab.
m: : the one who has no stuffing (

c: I was told from al-Ḥusayn, he said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd told us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say.
m: : the one who has no cavity. [Fn 2]

c: al-ʿAbbās b. Abī Ṭālib told me, he said: Muḥammad b. ʿUmar b. Rūmī told us, from ʿUbayd Allāh b. Saʿīd, the guide of al-Aʿmash, he said: Ṣāliḥ b. Ḥayyān told me, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Buraydah, from his father; he said: "I know only that he raised it" [to the Prophet ﷺ].
Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Bishr b. al-Mufaḍḍal told us, from al-Rabīʿ b. Muslim, he said: I heard al-Ḥasan say.
m: : the one who has no cavity. [Fn 4]

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from ʿIkrima.
m: : the one who has no cavity. [Fn 5]

x: Others said: it is the one from whom nothing issues.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Yaʿqūb told me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayya told us, from Abū Rajāʾ, he said: I heard ʿIkrima.
m: : the one from whom nothing has issued, who has not begotten and has not been begotten. [Fn 1]

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: Muḥammad b. Jaʿfar told us, he said: Shuʿba told us, from Abū Rajāʾ Muḥammad b. Yūsuf, from ʿIkrima.
m: : the one from whom nothing issues. [Fn 2]

x: Others said: it is the one who has not begotten and has not been begotten.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Abū Jaʿfar, from al-Rabīʿ, from Abū al-ʿĀliya.
m: : the one who has not begotten and has not been begotten, because there is nothing [that begets except that it will be inherited from] [Fn 3], and nothing that is begotten except that it will die. So He, exalted be His mention, informed them that He is not inherited from and does not die. [Fn 3]

c: Aḥmad b. Manīʿ and Maḥmūd b. Khidāsh told us, both said: [Abū Saʿd al-Ṣaghānī] [Fn 4] told us.
m: He said: The polytheists said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Trace for us your Lord." So God sent down:
Say: He is God, One (1) God, the
(2) He neither begets nor is begotten
, because there is nothing begotten that will not die, and nothing that dies that will not be inherited from; and God, glorified be His mention, does not die and is not inherited from.
And there is none comparable to Him
: no likeness and no equal to Him, and there is nothing like Him. [Fn 1 (p. 735)]
b.via: Abū Saʿd al-Ṣaghānī [the isnād continues as in Report 1, p. 727]

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us, from Abū Maʿshar, from Muḥammad b. Kaʿb.
m: : the one who has not begotten and has not been begotten, and there is none comparable to Him. [Fn 2]

x: Others said: it is the master (
Mention of those who said this:

c: Abū al-Sāʾib told me, he said: Abū Muʿāwiya told me, from al-Aʿmash, from Shaqīq.
m: : the master whose mastery has reached its limit. [Fn 3]

c: Abū Kurayb, Ibn Bashshār and Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, all said: Wakīʿ told us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Wāʾil.
m: : the master whose mastery has reached its limit. Abū Kurayb and Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā did not say "his mastery." [Fn 4]

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Wāʾil.
ʿAlī told us, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiya told me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
m: , he says: the master who is perfect in his mastery; the noble one who is perfect in his nobility; the great one who is perfect [Fn 2] in his greatness; the forbearing one who is perfect in his forbearance; the rich one who is perfect in his richness; the Compeller who is perfect in His compulsion; the knowing one who is perfect in his knowledge; and the wise one who is perfect in his wisdom. He is the one who is perfect in the kinds of nobility and mastery, and He is God, glorified be He. This is His attribute, which is not fitting for anyone but Him. [Fn 3]

x: Others said: rather it is the Enduring who does not perish.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda.
m: Say: He is God, One (1) God, the
(2) He neither begets nor is begotten
, he said: al-Ḥasan and Qatāda used to say: "the One who endures after His creation." He said: This is a sincere (
) sūra, with no mention in it of anything of the affairs of this world or the next. [Fn 4]

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda.

x: , among the Arabs, is the master to whom one turns (
), above whom there is no one; so they call their nobles by this. Of this is the saying of the poet [Fn 1]:

lines: Behold, the announcer of death came early, with the news of the two best of Banū Asad,
ʿAmr b. Masʿūd and the master, the
and no pledge is given except by a master, a

x: That being so, what is most fitting for the interpretation of the word is the meaning known from the speech of the people in whose tongue the Qurʾān was revealed. Had the ḥadīth of Ibn Buraydah from his father been sound, it would have been the soundest of the views, because the Messenger of God ﷺ knows best what God, glorified be His mention, meant and what He revealed to him.
. He says: He is not perishing, for nothing begets except it is perishing and ephemeral.

: He says: He is not originated, having not been and then come to be; for everything begotten has come into existence after not being, and has come into being after it was non-existent. Rather He, exalted be His mention, is eternal (
) [Fn 3], ever existing, and everlasting, [who does not perish] [Fn 4], does not pass away and does not cease to be.
and there is none comparable to Him
The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of this.
Some of them said: its meaning is that He has no likeness [Fn 1] and no equal.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Abū Jaʿfar, from al-Rabīʿ, from Abū al-ʿĀliya.
m: and there is none comparable to Him
: He has no likeness [Fn 1] and no equal, and there is nothing like Him. [Fn 2]

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda, from ʿAmr b. Ghaylān al-Thaqafī, who was the governor of Basra, from Kaʿb.
m: He said: God, exalted be His mention, founded the seven heavens and the seven earths on this sūra:
He has not begotten and was not begotten (2) and there is none comparable to Him (3)
. And no one among His creation matches God. [Fn 3]

c: ʿAlī told me, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiya told me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
m: And there is none comparable to Him
: he said: There is nothing like Him; glory be to God, the One, the Subduer. [Fn 4]

c: al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Waraqāʾ told us, from Ibn Jurayj [Fn 5].

Mention of those who said this:

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told us, he said: Sufyān told us, from ʿAbd al-Malik b. Abjar, from Ṭalḥa, from Mujāhid.
m: and there is none comparable to Him

Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Idrīs told us, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from Ṭalḥa, from Mujāhid.
Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Ibn Abjar, from a man, from Mujāhid.
m: And there is none comparable to Him

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us, from Sufyān, from ʿAbd al-Malik b. Abjar, from Ṭalḥa b. Muṣarrif, from Mujāhid.
m: And there is none comparable to Him

c: Abū al-Sāʾib told us, he said: Ibn Idrīs told us, from ʿAbd al-Malik, from Ṭalḥa, from Mujāhid.

notes.en: M reads “Saʿīd al-Ṣanʿānī.” See Tahdhīb al-kamāl, 33/346.
notes.ar: في م: "سعيد الصنعاني". وينظر تهذيب الكمال 33/ 346.

notes.en: Ibn Taymiyya cites it from the author in Majmūʿ al-fatāwā, 17/222. Ibn Khuzayma in al-Tawḥīd, p. 30, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim (as cited in Majmūʿ al-fatāwā, 17/221) reported it through Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ and Maḥmūd ibn Khidāsh. Al-Dārimī in al-Radd ʿalā al-jahmiyya, p. 7; al-Tirmidhī (3364); al-ʿUqaylī in al-Ḍuʿafāʾ, 4/141; Ibn ʿAdī in al-Kāmil, 6/2231–2232; al-Wāḥidī in Asbāb al-nuzūl, p. 346; al-Bayhaqī in al-Asmāʾ wa-l-ṣifāt (607); and al-Khaṭīb in Tārīkh Baghdād, 3/281, reported it through Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ. Aḥmad, 5/133–134; al-Bukhārī in al-Tārīkh al-kabīr, 1/245; Ibn Abī ʿĀṣim in al-Sunna (663); and Abū al-Shaykh in al-ʿAẓama (90) reported it through Abū Saʿd. Al-Ḥākim, 2/540, and through him al-Bayhaqī in al-Iʿtiqād, p. 38, reported it through Abū Jaʿfar.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن تيمية في مجموع الفتاوى 17/ 222 عن المصنف، وأخرجه ابن خزيمة في التوحيد ص 30، وابن أبي حاتم - كما في مجموع الفتاوى 17/ 221 - من طريق أحمد بن منيع ومحمود بن خداش به، وأخرجه الدارمي في الرد على الجهمية ص 7، والترمذى (3364)، والعقيلي في الضعفاء 4/ 141، وابن عدى في الكامل 6/ 2231، 2232، والواحدي في أسباب النزول ص 346، والبيهقي في الأسماء والصفات (607)، والخطيب في تاريخ بغداد 3/ 281 من طريق أحمد بن منيع به، وأخرجه أحمد 5/ 133، 134، والبخاري في التاريخ الكبير 1/ 245، وابن أبي عاصم في السنة (663)، وأبو الشيخ في العظمة (90) من طريق أبي سعد به، وأخرجه الحاكم 2/ 540، وعنه البيهقي في الاعتقاد ص 38،=

notes.en: Al-Ḥākim, 2/540, and through him al-Bayhaqī in al-Iʿtiqād, p. 38, al-Asmāʾ wa-l-ṣifāt (50), and Shuʿab al-īmān (101), reported it through Abū Jaʿfar.
notes.ar: = والأسماء والصفات (50)، والشعب (101) من طريق أبي جعفر به.

notes.en: M, T1, T2, and T3 read “the Messenger of God.”
notes.ar: في م، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3: "رسول اللَّهِ".

notes.en: Ibn Taymiyya cites it from the author in Majmūʿ al-fatāwā, 17/222; al-Suyūṭī attributes it to al-Muṣannaf in al-Durr al-manthūr, 6/410.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن تيمية في مجموع الفتاوى 17/ 222 عن المصنف، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 410 إلى المصنف.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributes it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 6/410, to al-Muṣannaf and Ibn al-Ḍurays, as a statement of Abū al-ʿĀliya. It is in Ibn al-Ḍurays’s Faḍāʾil al-Qurʾān (244), through Abū Jaʿfar from al-Rabīʿ, as his statement.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 410 إلى المصنف وابن الضريس من قول أبي العالية، وهو عند ابن الضريس في فضائل القرآن (244) من طريق أبي جعفر، عن الربيع قوله.

notes.en: M reads “Shurayj.” See Tahdhīb al-kamāl, 3/185.
notes.ar: في م: "شريج". وينظر تهذيب الكمال 3/ 185.

notes.en: Cited by Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr, 8/538, from al-Muṣannaf. Abū Yaʿlā (2044), ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad in al-Sunna (1185), al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ (5687), Ibn ʿAdī in al-Kāmil, 1/313, Abū Nuʿaym in Ḥilyat al-awliyāʾ, 4/335, al-Bayhaqī in al-Asmāʾ wa-l-ṣifāt (608), and al-Wāḥidī in Asbāb al-nuzūl, p. 346, reported it through Ismāʿīl ibn Mujālid. Al-Suyūṭī attributes it to Ibn al-Mundhir in al-Durr al-manthūr, 6/410.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 8/ 538 عن المصنف، وأخرجه أبو يعلى (2044)، وعبد اللَّهِ بن أحمد في السنة (1185)، والطبرانى في الأوسط (5687)، وابن عدى في الكامل 1/ 313، وأبو نعيم في الحلية 4/ 335، والبيهقي في الأسماء والصفات (608)، والواحدى في أسباب النزول ص 346 من طريق إسماعيل بن مجالد به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 410 إلى ابن المنذر.

notes.en: That is, his face changed color. The expression is used when one’s color changes from fear, pain, or similar causes. Al-Nihāya, 5/109.
notes.ar: أي تغير وجهه. يقال: انتقع لونه وامتقع، إذا تغير من خوف أو ألم أو نحو ذلك. النهاية 5/ 109.

notes.en: The use of “the Pre-eternal” as an attribute of God is questionable. The Qurʾān and sound Sunna do not use this attribute of God; the term used to express its meaning is “the First,” as in “He is the First and the Last” [Qurʾān 57:3]. The Prophet’s supplication likewise says: “O God, You are the First, and there was nothing before You; You are the Last, and there is nothing after You,” reported by Muslim (2713). Theologians introduced this term among the names of God, but it is not one of the Most Beautiful Names, since it implies time: if He is “ancient,” one might ask what is “more ancient.” The Qurʾānic and Prophetic term “the First” is more precise. See Sharḥ al-ʿaqīda al-ṭaḥāwiyya, 1/75–77.
notes.ar: في إطلاق صفة "القديم" على الله نظر. فهذه صفة لم يرد إطلاقها على الله سبحانه وتعالى في القرآن الكريم ولا في السنة الصحيحة، وإنما الذي ورد للتعبير عن معناها لفظ (الأول)، كما قال الله سبحانه: {هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ} [الحديد: 3]. وقول النبي عمل في ثنائه على الله سبحانه: "اللهم أنت الأول فليس قبلك شيء، وأنت الآخر فليس بعدك شيء". أخرجه مسلم (2713). فهذا اللفظ مما أدخله المتكلمون في أسماء الله تعالى وليس هو من الأسماء الحسنى؛ وذلك لأنه يحتوى على معنى الزمن، فإذا كان "قديما" فهناك "أقدم" قياسا على صيغة أفعل، أما لفظ القرآن والسنة "الأول" فكان أدق في التعبير. ينظر شرح العقيدة الطحاوية 1/ 75 - 77.

notes.en: Abū al-Shaykh in al-ʿAẓama (895) reported it through Saʿīd; Abū Nuʿaym, 5/383, through Qatāda; and Ibn al-Ḍurays in Faḍāʾil al-Qurʾān (246), briefly, through Qatāda from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ghālib from Kaʿb. Ibn Abī Ḥātim (as cited in Majmūʿ al-fatāwā, 17/222) reported it through Yazīd from Saʿīd from Qatāda, quoting only the ending.
notes.ar: أخرجه أبو الشيخ في العظمة (895) من طريق سعيد به، وأخرجه أبو نعيم 5/ 383 من طريق قتادة به، وأخرجه ابن الضريس في فضائل القرآن (246) من طريق قتادة عن عبد الله بن غالب عن كعب مختصرا، وأخرجه ابن أبي حاتم - كما في مجموع الفتاوى 17/ 222 - من طريق يزيد، عن سعيد، عن قتادة قوله مقتصرا على آخره.

notes.en: The source references were given above, p. 736.
notes.ar: تقدم تخريجه في ص 736.

notes.en: T1 reads “Abū Najīḥ”; T2 and T3 read “Abū Najīḥ from Mujāhid.”
notes.ar: في ت 1: "أبي نجيح"، وفى ت 2 ت 3: "أبي نجيح عن مجاهد".

notes.en: Abū Nuʿaym reported it in Ḥilyat al-awliyāʾ, 3/300, through Yaḥyā.
notes.ar: أخرجه أبو نعيم في الحلية 3/ 300 من طريق يحيى به.

notes.en: His Dīwān, p. 21.
notes.ar: ديوانه ص 21.

notes.en: Taʾaththafūhu means “they surrounded him.” Lisān al-ʿArab, root (أ ث ف).
notes.ar: تأثَّفوه: تكنَّفُوه. اللسان (أ ث ف).

notes.en: Ḥafṣ read kufuʾan (with ḍamma on fāʾ); Ḥamza, Khalaf, and Yaʿqūb read kufʾan (with sukūn on fāʾ); the others read kufuʾan (with ḍamma and hamza). See al-Nashr, 2/162.
notes.ar: قرأ حفص (كُفُوًا)، وقرأ حمزة وخلف ويعقوب (كُفْئًا)، وقرأ الباقون (كُفُؤًا). ينظر النشر 2/ 162.
